data.title: Utilities Shares Tick Higher as Energy Rally Cools — Utilities Roundup
data.description:
Shares of utility companies pared weekly losses as energy costs stabilized around elevated levels and the rapid rise in Treasury yields cooled a bit.

Oil prices fell as investors assessed prospects for U.S.-Iran diplomacy aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, U.S. natural-gas futures pared gains that were due to the outage on a pipeline in West Virginia operated by a unit of TC Energy.

While no date for a resumption of service had been given, the fact the problem was confined to the regulator station "reduced concern that the outage will require a prolonged pipeline-integrity response," Gelber & Associates said in a note. LNG feedgas flows continue to support market balances, "but cooling demand is declining as the market moves deeper into the shoulder season," the firm added.

data.title: Boo in the Bottoms Awakens Halloween in Kansas City from Daytime Delights to Nighttime Frights
data.description:
Boo in the Bottoms Awakens Halloween in Kansas City from Daytime Delights to Nighttime Frights

Boo in the Bottoms Awakens Halloween in Kansas City from Daytime Delights to Nighttime Frights

PR Newswire

KANSAS CITY, Mo., Sept. 25, 2026

Beast and Edge of Hell Open for the Season as Festival of the Full Moon
Celebrates Boo in the Bottoms, October 2-4

KANSAS CITY, Mo., Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Halloween officially comes alive in Kansas City when the Historic West Bottoms celebrates Boo in the Bottoms during First Friday Weekend, October 2-4. This year's event brings a new twist as the daytime festival, filled with shopping, music, Thriller-themed dance instruction, costumed characters, and family fun, transforms into a nighttime destination for thrill-seekers when legendary haunted attractions Beast and Edge of Hell open their 2026 seasons on Friday, October 2.

Daytime treats: the West Bottoms is filled with treasure hunters searching for vintage finds, seasonal décor, antiques, gifts, and one-of-a-kind discoveries across 13 blocks of historic buildings. Costumed visitors can trick-or-treat at participating stores, gather around boo-tiful fire pits for s'mores, enjoy festive drinks from the Full Moon Street Bar, and meet friendly haunt characters roaming the district for photos and laughs.

Music in the streets adds to the fall atmosphere, while on Saturday from 11 a.m -2 p.m, visitors can also learn the iconic moves to Michael Jackson's "Thriller" during free, special dance instruction sessions led by D3 Stepper, creating a playful celebration for anyone who wants to join in the famous zombie moves. Bring the kids to trick-or-treat in participating stores.

"Boo in the Bottoms is when we kick off Halloween Kansas City-style," said Amber Arnett-Bequeaith, Queen of Haunts and spokesperson for the district. "Come down during the day and get into some good trouble. Hunt for vintage treasures, learn the 'Thriller' dance or watch the dancers, and get your picture with our haunt characters before they go to work. Then Friday night, things take a darker turn. Beast and Edge of Hell open their doors for the season, and after that, you're on your own. With only 13 October nights to get your haunt fix, maybe 13 isn't unlucky after all. It's time to stir the cauldron, make some memories, and find out why generations of Kansas Citians keep coming back to get scared."

The same streets where shoppers searched for treasures become the gateway to two of Kansas City's legendary haunted attractions, turning the district from vintage to vampires, from treats to terrors, and from shopping destination to Halloween headquarters.

BOO IN THE BOTTOMS WEEKEND PLANNER

  • West Bottoms Shopping — West Bottoms Shopping — More than 30 stores, restaurants, and entertainment venues will be open throughout the Festival of the Full Moon weekend. Most shops are open from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Friday and Saturday and 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sunday. Hours vary by business.

Featured Businesses — Throughout the 13-block district, visitors will find a mix of shopping, dining, and entertainment.

  • All Keyed Up Piano Shop – www.allkeyeduppiano.com
  • Amigoni Urban Winery – www.amigoni.com
  • Bella Patina www.bellapatinakc.com
  • Brass Pig
  • Chef J's Barbecue www.chefjbbq.com
  • Good JuJuwww.goodjujukc.com
  • Java Garage www.thejavagarage.com
  • Robins Nest www.facebook.com/therobinsnestwestbottoms
  • Rustic Vintage Rose www.facebook.com/RusticVintageRose
  • Serendipity 
  • Treasures on 13th 2 stores, 2nd floor and street level in the Central Bag Building www.facebook.com/treasureson13thstKC
  • Ugly Glasswww.facebook.com/UglyGlassCo
  • Charmed House www.charmedhouseinteriors.com
  • West Bottoms Whiskey Co - www.westbottomswhiskey
  • Halloween Fun & Meet-and-Greet Haunt Characters — Family-friendly scare cast members will roam outside Friday and Saturday from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and Sunday from noon to 3 p.m. Guests are encouraged to wear costumes, take photos, and trick-or-treat at participating stores.
  • Street Music & Thriller Dance Instruction — Enjoy live entertainment in the streets and learn the famous "Thriller" dance at no cost for a fun led by dance instructor D3 Stepper, this is an interactive zombie groove experience for all ages. Saturday 11- 2 p.m.
  • Food & Drink — Indulge at Chef J BBQ, Java Garage, Bella Patina's Painted Rooster Café, West Bottoms Whiskey, and the Full Moon Street Bar.
  • Fire Pits & Full Moon Street Bar — Gather around glowing fire pits with your boo, roast s'mores, sip seasonal beverages, and enjoy the fall atmosphere. Available Friday, Saturday and Sunday 9-5pm
  • Haunted Attractions Opening Night — Beast and Edge of Hell open for the 2026 season beginning Friday, October 2, with a total of just 13 nights scheduled throughout October. Visit attraction websites for dates, times, and tickets. www.kcbeast.comwww.edgeofhell.com
  • KC Collectors Spooky Plant Sale — Saturday, October 3, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. - featuring plant vendors, Halloween-themed items, candy, costumes, and collectibles.

This year, Beast and Edge of Hell have just 13 nights on the October schedule, followed by the remaining 2026 West Bottoms First Friday Weekend events: Blessings in the Bottoms, Nov. 6-8, and Bows in the Bottoms, each weekend in December prior to Christmas, beginning Dec. 4-6.

About the Historic West Bottoms Entertainment District

The Historic West Bottoms Entertainment District, located just off the 12th Street Bridge, encompasses a 13-block district of historic warehouses filled with hundreds of vendors, shops, restaurants, and entertainment venues. The district's multi-story buildings date back well over a century. These repurposed, vast spaces form the largest indoor vintage entertainment district operating year-round. The West Bottoms is the destination for interior decorators, designers, collectors, and consumers seeking stylish décor and gift options with a one-of-a-kind history and patina. westbottoms.com

data.title: Financial Shares Rise as Bonds Selloff Pauses — Financials Roundup
data.description:
Shares in the financial sector rose alongside U.S. stock indexes as this week's rise in interest rates took a break.

The economy kept showing signs of resilience, ahead of next week's key inflation and employment indicators.

Blackstone's top private-equity executive, Joseph Baratta, is preparing to leave the firm, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest in a series of departures by senior leaders from the private-investment giant. Baratta, who has been with Blackstone for nearly three decades, has been the firm's global head of private equity since 2012 and is one of its most senior executives. He is also a Blackstone board member and part of the firm's management committee. The exact timing of his departure hasn't been determined, but it is likely to come around the end of this year, the people said.

data.title: Materials Shares Rise as Metal Prices Tick Higher — Materials Roundup
data.description:
Producers of metals, grains and other raw materials rose as gold futures snapped a four-session losing streak as the U.S. dollar pulled back following four straight sessions of gains. Silver and copper also rose.

ArcelorMittal said it cannot safely restart operations at its Ukrainian subsidiary after missile attacks killed five people and injured 17 employees, and expects to record a $1 billion impairment. The Luxembourg-based steelmaker said Friday that four missile strikes at ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih over the past five weeks also caused extensive damage to production facilities. The most recent attack was on Monday. The expected noncash impairment charge mainly relates to damaged property, plant and equipment at the site in Kryvyi Rih, central Ukraine.

Largo shares were sharply lower Friday after the company priced its $5.7 million offering below recent trading prices. The Canadian miner on Friday said it would offer 10.2 million units at a price of 56 cents apiece.

data.title: Industrial Shares Among Top Gainers Amid Signs of Resilient Economy — Industrials Roundup
data.description:
A broad recovery in U.S. stock markets lifted shares in the industrial sector. Economic indicators have pointed to resilient growth despite elevated borrowing costs.

Demand for U.S. durable goods was unchanged in August, according to data published by the Commerce Department, beating forecasts of a small contraction. Total orders for durable goods decreased $0.1 billion in August to $338.6 billion, following a 0.9% July increase. Transportation equipment, down three of the last four months, drove the decrease, falling 0.6%. Excluding defense, new orders increased 0.1%.

Bloom Energy jumped Friday after a Wall Street firm reassured investors that the company won't be affected by Oracle's push to protect itself against potential delays on its massive data-center project. Oracle sent a force majeure notice Thursday to Stack Infrastructure, the developer of its Project Jupiter campus in New Mexico, Bloomberg reported.

Corecivic said its president and chief executive has resigned, citing health reasons. The private prison operator before the bell said Patrick Swindle, who is pursuing treatment for stage-four metastatic pancreatic cancer, would step down after less than a year at the helm. He has also resigned from the company's board.

Tesla will begin deliveries of its all-electric Semi truck to customers this week, after years of delays. The heavy-duty Semi was announced by Elon Musk in November 2017. At the time, the company had plans to kick off production a few years later. However, the company repeatedly pushed back the launch, preventing it from being able to serve the long-haul freight market on its original timeline.

data.description:
HILLSIDE, NJ / ACCESS Newswire / September 25, 2026 / Integrated BioPharma, Inc. (OTCQX:INBP) (the "Company" or "INBP") reports its financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended June 30, 2026.

Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $9.8 million compared to $14.2 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, a decrease of $4.4 million or 31.0%. The Company had an operating loss of $0.9 million compared to operating income of approximately $0.6 million in the quarters ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Revenues for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 were $43.9 million compared to $54.4 million for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, a decrease of $10.5 million or 19.3%. The Company had an operating loss for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 of approximately $2.7 million compared to operating income of $2.0 million for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025.

For the quarters ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company had a net loss of approximately $1.4 million and $0.2 million or $0.04 and $0.01 per share of common stock, respectively. The Company's diluted net loss per share of common stock for the quarters ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 were $0.04 and $0.01 per share of common stock, respectively.

For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, the Company had a net loss of approximately $2.8 million or $0.09 per share of common stock, compared with net income of approximately $0.8 million or $0.03 per share of common stock for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025. The Company's diluted net (loss) income per share of common stock for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 were ($0.09) and $0.03 per share of common stock, respectively.
